chunks: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh said: Muhammad ibn Hammam ibn Suhayl narrated to me from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Ghazzari, who said: Muhammad ibn Hamdan al-Mad'ini narrated to us from Ziyad al-Qandi, who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'O Ziyad, I love for you what I love for myself, and I dislike for you what I dislike for myself. Perfect the prayer in the two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), in Kufa, and at the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَن: Abu al-Hasan, a title for an Imam
key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: The two Sanctuaries, referring to Mecca and Medina
key_terms.الْكُوفَة: Kufa, a major city in Iraq with significant Shia historical importance

ai.seo_question: What are the specific locations where the prayer should be perfected according to this hadith from Imam al-Hassan?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (Abu al-Hasan) advises Ziyad al-Qandi to perfect his prayers in the two major Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), Kufa, and specifically at the grave of Imam al-Husayn, highlighting the spiritual merit of these locations. The opening phrase 'I love for you what I love for myself' underscores the Imam’s personal endorsement of this practice, linking it to the broader Shia tradition of visiting shrines (Ziyarat) as acts of devotion. This instruction reflects the scholarly view that while prayer is obligatory everywhere, its reward is magnified in these specific holy sites, particularly Karbala, which holds a unique status in Shia piety.
